analysis.headline: Shares Your Data for Ads
analysis.quote: Our advertisers ask us to use reader data so their ads can be targeted at the right audiences.

analysis.headline: Shares Your Data Online
analysis.quote: When we detect a GPC signal from a reader’s browser where GDPR, CCPA or a similar privacy law applies, we stop sharing the reader’s personal data online with other companies (except with our service providers).

analysis.headline: Collects Your Behavioral Data
analysis.quote: Our tracking technologies collect data about your reading behavior, like which articles you read, which recipes you save, which Games you play or how often you visit The Times.

analysis.headline: Collects Your Data From Third-Parties
analysis.quote: Additionally, we collect data about readers from sources like privately owned databases and social media platforms.

analysis.headline: Targets You With Ads
analysis.quote: For example, we use readers’ data to identify who may be interested in a subscription in order to show you Times ads on other websites.

analysis.headline: No Data Deletion Info
analysis.quote: This F.A.Q. applies to nytimes.com readers.

analysis.headline: Supports Global Privacy Control
analysis.quote: Yes. When we detect a GPC signal from a reader’s browser where GDPR, CCPA or a similar privacy law applies, we stop sharing the reader’s personal data online with other companies (except with our service providers).
